methodology.observation_window_basis: Window starts at the latest successful immutable run's window_end and ends at the current pre-schedule observation cutoff.
methodology.ranking_basis: Signal strength rather than popularity, emphasizing difficult-to-reverse commercialization, deployment, manufacturing, infrastructure, strategic partnerships, regulatory progress, and meaningful technical milestones.
methodology.source_policy: Prefer primary company, government, regulatory, and research-institution sources; use originating-company releases distributed by reputable wire services when needed.
methodology.repeat_policy: Canonical event fingerprints were checked; repeated events are included only for material updates with preserved event_key and material_update_from.
excluded_noise: market-price movement without underlying technical or commercial change

provenance.notes: Publication-request branch handoff; legacy history and longitudinal visual were not used.

findings.headline: Huawei commercializes LogicFolding chip architecture in the Mate 90 flagship line
findings.summary: Huawei launched the Mate 90 series with its self-developed Tau/Kirin chipset family, including the Kirin 9050 Pro using a LogicFolding architecture that restructures chip wiring in 3D; Huawei says the new platform is vertically integrated with HarmonyOS 7 and its broader hardware and cloud stack.
findings.why_it_matters: Shipping a new domestic chip architecture in a mass-market flagship is a concrete commercialization milestone for China's effort to improve compute performance despite constrained access to leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing.
findings.trend_statement: Semiconductor constraints are pushing vertically integrated device makers toward architectural and packaging innovation rather than relying only on process-node scaling.

source_links.title: Huawei Launches the HUAWEI Mate 90 Series, Equipped with the Flagship Tau Chipset Across the Entire Series

findings.headline: Mendaera commercializes Butterfly Ultrasound-on-Chip imaging in its FDA-cleared Focalist robotic intervention system
findings.summary: Mendaera and Butterfly Network announced commercial availability of a Butterfly-compatible Focalist system, combining handheld robotics, real-time ultrasound imaging and guidance software for image-guided needle procedures; it is the first Butterfly Embedded partner technology to reach the market.
findings.why_it_matters: This moves semiconductor-based ultrasound from a standalone imaging device into a commercially available robotic intervention platform, creating a programmable sensing layer for future AI-assisted procedural action.
findings.trend_statement: Medical robotics is integrating software-defined semiconductor sensing directly into intervention platforms, narrowing the gap between imaging, guidance and robotic action.

source_links.title: Mendaera’s Focalist System Now Compatible with Butterfly’s Ultrasound-on-Chip Technology

findings.headline: SEMIFIVE and Mobilint sign turnkey contract to commercialize a robotics AI chip under Korea's on-device semiconductor program
findings.summary: SEMIFIVE signed a turnkey development contract with Mobilint for an on-device robotics AI chip under South Korea's government-funded K-On-Device AI Semiconductor Technology Development program. The design targets outdoor robotic operation and will integrate LPDDR6, PCIe Gen6 and UCIe-S, with SEMIFIVE responsible from detailed design through packaging, testing and mass production.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract moves physical-AI silicon beyond general edge accelerators toward application-specific robotics hardware with a defined path through manufacturing and commercialization.
findings.trend_statement: Physical AI is creating demand for specialized on-device compute architectures optimized for robotic sensing, control, power efficiency and disconnected operation.

source_links.title: SEMIFIVE Signs Turnkey Contract with Mobilint to Develop Robotics AI Chip Under 'K-On-Device AI Semiconductor' Program

findings.headline: Agility and FORT formalize offboard safety architecture for Digit 5 humanoid deployments
findings.summary: Agility Robotics and FORT Robotics signed an MOU expanding their multi-year work into a three-part safety architecture for Digit 5: a safety pendant, on-robot communications and off-robot interfaces connecting Digit with external safety systems. The agreement also covers joint hardware development, regulatory compliance and deployment support as Digit 5 moves into more complex commercial environments.
findings.why_it_matters: Humanoid deployment at scale depends on safety infrastructure that extends beyond onboard perception and control. Formalizing an interoperable offboard safety layer is a concrete step toward operating humanoids near people in warehouses, manufacturing and logistics.
findings.trend_statement: Commercial humanoid robotics is shifting from robot-only safety toward layered facility-level safety and regulatory infrastructure.

source_links.title: Agility and FORT Robotics Announce Strategic Partnership to Advance Humanoid Robot Safety
